title: Introduce lint executor plugin and dynamic test catalog
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduces a plugin-based lint executor and a dynamic test catalog for path-aware test selection. Improves CI feedback speed for small changes and enables teams to add custom check adapters without repo changes.
description:
Motivation: Our lint/test pipeline has grown multiple ad-hoc handlers for different languages and repositories. Adding new checks requires repo changes and CI config churn. Small change PRs still pay the full test/lint cost which increases build time and flakiness.

Summary: Adds a lightweight plugin system for the lint executor and a dynamic test catalog that maps changed paths to a curated set of checks. The plugin system lets teams register adapters (e.g., terraform, rustfmt, go vet, custom schema validators) without modifying the core runner. The dynamic catalog lives in a yaml manifest (test-catalog.yaml) and can be updated independently; CI computes which catalog entries apply to the PR and runs only the matching shards.

What changed (high level):
- New executor: internal/ci/lint/executor is now a plugin host which loads adapters from plugins/ (adapters are small node/ts or go shims).
- Dynamic catalog: ci/catalog/test-catalog.yaml introduced with rules (path globs, label hints, priority).
- CI pipeline: .github/workflows/ci-lint.yml updated to call the catalog resolver step and then spawn only required shards.
- Backwards compatibility shim: existing lint-wrapper scripts remain available for a transitional period; the plugin host can execute them via the provided shell adapter.
- Tooling: small CLI (bin/catalog-resolve) added to evaluate applicable catalog entries locally for debugging.
- Docs: docs/ci/plugin-runner.md and docs/ci/test-catalog.md with examples and migration guide.

Commits summary:
- a1b4c9d: scaffold plugin host and runtime API, basic lifecycle hooks (register, run, report).
- b2d33ea: add test-catalog schema and resolver CLI + unit tests.
- f7e9112: integrate catalog resolver into github action, update workflow to emit selected shards.
- 9c4b2fa: add node adapter shim for eslint/tslint + sample plugin.
- d4f011b: docs and migration guide, examples for OSS and internal teams.

Files changed (not exhaustive):
- internal/ci/lint/executor/host.go
- internal/ci/lint/adapter_interface.md
- plugins/node-eslint/adapter.ts
- ci/catalog/test-catalog.yaml
- .github/workflows/ci-lint.yml
- bin/catalog-resolve (executable)
- docs/ci/plugin-runner.md
- docs/ci/test-catalog.md

Testing & CI:
- Unit tests for the resolver and host (internal/ci/lint/*) added and passing.
- Integration smoke GitHub Action that runs the resolver on a synthetic changeset (added as a job in ci-lint.yml).
- Initial run flagged an environment-related flake in the adapter shim on Ubuntu-latest (node 18 vs node 20 mismatch). I updated the adapter to use nvm-run and pinned the action runner versions; rerun succeeded.

Review thread (high-level):
- Priya: Requested clearer upgrade path for internal teams that rely on custom scripts; I added the compatibility shim and documented the migration steps.
- Tom: Asked for telemetry points to measure adoption and skipped checks; added instrumentation hooks and a lightweight metric emission via the existing CI telemetry pipeline.
- Evan: Called out potential security implications of third-party plugins; we added a plugin vetting checklist to docs and limited host permissions (plugins run in a restricted sandboxed process).

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind the feature-flag CI_LINT_PLUGIN=on.
2) Enable for a single small repo (benchmark-lab) for 2 weeks and monitor shard selection coverage and CI time reduction.
3) Gradually onboard other repos and maintainers; plugin registry entries for internal adapters stored under plugins/ with PR review + vetting procedure.

Migration notes for consumers:
- To add a custom adapter, create a plugin under plugins/<name>/ with the adapter entrypoint and a short adapter.yaml describing inputs/outputs. See docs/ci/plugin-runner.md.
- Existing lint scripts will continue to run via the shell adapter; convert them incrementally to plugin adapters to get faster shard-level parallelism.

Operational considerations:
- Telemetry: counts of resolved catalog entries per PR, average CI time per shard, and skipped checks will be emitted (tagged by repo and catalog entry).
- Security: plugins are executed with limited environment variables and no network access by default; maintainers may request explicit allowances.
- Failure modes: if the resolver fails, the job falls back to the legacy full-lint job to ensure correctness (fail-open disabled).

Why this is different from previous work: Instead of hardcoding language handlers or expanding workflow permutations, this provides an extensible catalog and a lightweight plugin surface so teams can add checks without changing core CI logic. It targets the long tail of repo-specific linters and reduces unnecessary CI work for small changes.

Notes: The PR intentionally keeps the resolver implementation simple (no evaluation of complex expressions) to reduce surprises. Future work can add a remote catalog service and UI in the Console for global rules management.

If anything should be trimmed before rollout (e.g., remove sample node plugin), let me know and I can open a follow-up to strip samples post-adoption.
